Hi Jonas,

Our security team is finalizing the dedicated deployment checklist and has a couple of specific asks around regional anchoring and deletion guarantees before we move the contract to procurement. Can you provide the following evidence for our in-country requirement?

- A short attestation that tenant data for our Dedicated cluster is pinned to the US region and will not be replicated outside the region under normal operation.
- Sample logs or a redacted runbook showing the steps performed when a tenant is deprovisioned (data sweep / KV cache purge / snapshot removal).
- Expected timeline for complete data redaction across replicas after a deprovision request (including snapshots and backups).
- Any interplay with legal hold or retention flags: if an enterprise legal hold is requested, how is deletion impacted?

We do not need raw logs — redacted samples and an attestation PDF are fine. If you can share these by Friday that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Maya Thompson

AtlasPay

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We can provide an attestation plus redacted sweep evidence and a retention matrix. Quick answers up front:

- Regional anchoring: we run AtlasPay on a US-dedicated pool; under normal operations we do not replicate tenant data to other regions. We will provide a signed attestation and a short technical appendix describing the non-replication guarantee.
- Deprovision sweep: standard process removes tenant objects, clears KV caches, and purges snapshots per the retention policy. I will attach a sanitized CSV that mirrors the actual sweep output.
- Timeline: typical full deletion across replicas is within 7 calendar days after the deprovision request completes; backups/snapshots are addressed per agreed retention windows — see matrix we will attach.
- Legal hold: if a legal hold is in effect we postpone irreversible deletion until the hold is lifted; we will include the retention/hold escalation flow.

Do you prefer the artifacts as PDF/CSV via Google Drive link or as email attachments? I can also schedule a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the appendices.

Regards,

Hi Maya — following up with the artifacts we discussed. Attaching a short attestation and redacted evidence set; summary below.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Attestation: attached "anchoring_attestation.pdf" (signed by Trust Operations) confirming AtlasPay tenant data for your Dedicated allocation is pinned to the US region and not replicated outside the US under normal operating conditions.
- Sweep sample: attached "sample_kv_sweep.csv" — redacted sample of the deprovision sweep that shows sequence of actions (cache invalidation, object tombstone, replica sweep). Identifiers are hashed; no customer PII included.
- Retention matrix: attached "retention_matrix.xlsx" — maps snapshots/backups, default retention windows, and deletion triggers.

Operational notes and timeline
- Deprovisioning: when Atlapay requests tenant deprovision we execute the sweep which marks objects for deletion, clears in-memory KV caches, and schedules snapshot deletions.
- Timeline to irreversible data removal: typical completion across the cluster and replica sets is within 7 calendar days after the deprovision job finishes. This covers live data, KV caches, and scheduled snapshot expiry actions.
- Backups/snapshots: snapshots are retained according to the retention matrix; snapshot destruction is performed automatically when the retention window expires or can be accelerated per customer request (subject to contractual terms).
- Legal hold: if a legal hold/retention flag is applied, irreversible deletion is paused until hold removal. We include a documented escalation path in the attestation appendix.

Next steps
- Deliverables: anchoring_attestation.pdf, sample_kv_sweep.csv, retention_matrix.xlsx (attached).
- If you want, we can do a 30-minute call next week to walk the Trust Ops attestation and the sweep sample. Proposed slots: Tue 27 May 10:00-10:30 ET or Wed 28 May 14:00-14:30 ET.

If this addresses your checklist we can mark the security item resolved and move to procurement.

Best,
